sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 1! Adjust element count N and condition number kappa. Compare naive summation error against Higham's theoretical bound and observe Kahan compensated summation.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, let's test our cluster! Notice how increasing condition number to one hundred thousand spikes naive error while Kahan summation remains perfectly stable.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1! Given N equals one million floats, sum of absolute gradients fifty thousand, and true sum zero point five, what is condition number kappa, Higham factor gamma, and the necessary mitigation?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1! Condition number is one hundred thousand, and Higham's error bound exceeds three thousand! Which option correctly identifies this divergence?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! Option A is correct. Condition number equals one hundred thousand and Higham factor gamma is zero point zero six three four, creating an error bound of over three thousand and relative error over six hundred thousand percent. Fixed tree reductions or Kahan sums are mandatory!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Remember condition number kappa is fifty thousand divided by zero point five, which equals one hundred thousand. Higham factor gamma times absolute sum bounds error to over three thousand, producing six hundred thousand percent relative error!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 2! Adjust true effect size delta, replication sample size n2, and FAIR compliance level. Observe the Winner's curse effect size inflation and the 4-axis compliance radar.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, look at the power readout! When initial effect size is zero point one five and replication size is one hundred, statistical power is only thirty-two percent. We need four hundred sixty-eight samples for ninety percent power!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2! Under selective publication with alpha zero point zero five, if true effect size is zero point one five with standard error zero point one zero, what is expected published effect, power for n equals one hundred, and required sample size for ninety percent power?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2! Calculating the inverse Mills ratio shows published effect is inflated to zero point two six one two, and replication power with n equals one hundred is only thirty-two percent. What is the required sample size?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Excellent! Option A is correct. The inverse Mills ratio inflates published effect size by seventy-four percent to zero point two six one two. Statistical power for sample size one hundred is only thirty-two point three percent, and ninety percent power requires four hundred sixty-eight patients!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Under publication filtering at Z equals one point nine six, cutoff tau equals zero point four six, giving an inverse Mills ratio of one point one one. The published effect is inflated to zero point two six one two, and ninety percent power requires four hundred sixty-eight samples.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 3! According to the Vines exponential decay law of seventeen percent annual loss, what is the survival probability of an unversioned lab dataset after ten years, and how do FAIR principles eliminate epistemic entropy?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 3! Raising zero point eight three to the tenth power gives fifteen point five percent. How does FAIR content-addressed storage guarantee scientific repeatability?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding mastery! Option A is correct. Survival probability drops to fifteen point five percent after ten years. FAIR persistent DOIs and content-addressed storage reduce conditional epistemic entropy to zero, guaranteeing permanent repeatability!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Vines empirical analysis demonstrated a seventeen percent annual decay rate, leaving only fifteen point five percent of datasets accessible after ten years. FAIR content-addressed storage with persistent DOIs is mandatory to prevent link rot.
